answer: At an island trade summit for umber pigment, the AI agents running the exchange require each seller identity to lock 100 tokens in escrow for 30 days before it can list goods. The same tokens cannot back multiple identities, so an attacker creating 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize 100,000 tokens for a month. New names are cheap, but the listing capacity they unlock carries a fixed capital cost, limiting how cheaply fake sellers can flood the market.
